Quick technical notes for the bundle — collating items here so Maya can paste to the client: 

- SBOM: we can produce both SPDX and CSV exports from our build artifacts pipeline. The SBOM will include sha256 checksums, package source URLs, and build-time provenance. File: sbom-redwood-202611.csv (will redact internal build node IPs).

- Model artifact provenance: we sign model weights and checkpoints using an internal signing service. Public verification steps (we will include in the packet):
  1) curl https://models.redwood.ai/checksums/<model-id>.sig | gpg --verify - 
  2) run sha256sum on the downloaded blob and compare to the verified manifest
  We will include the public key (redwood-models.pub) and sample commands.

- KMS/HSM: supported integrations: AWS KMS (CMKs), Azure Key Vault (BYOK), HashiCorp Vault w/ HSM plug-in. For isolated installs we support HSM appliances (Luna, nCipher) via PKCS#11 connector. Network requirement: outbound to key sync endpoints can be disabled for fully air-gapped (we support local key import and manual rotation scripts).

- Offline attestation & telemetry: for air-gapped installs we provide a signed attestation package generated on-site by the install operator; the package is a signed JSON blob that contains SBOM hash, runtime version, config digest, operator id, and timestamp. Telemetry is optional and can be disabled — we support an 'attestation-only' mode where the installer produces the signed attestation which we then verify out-of-band.

- Operator separation: RBAC model separates Installer (on-site operator with physical access), Deployment Admin (can start/stop runtime but cannot replace model artifacts), and Security Auditor (read-only access to logs and attestation reports). We will include operator-separation-diagram.pdf and a short CSV mapping tasks to roles.

- Patch SLA: standard scheduled updates quarterly. For critical security patches (CVSS >= 9.0) Redwood will provide: 
  * 48-hour mitigation guidance and hotfix script incrementally;
  * 14-day target for fully tested binaries and signed artifacts;
  * For on-prem customers, optional on-site EPC (Engineer for Patch Carryout) within customer SLA (additional professional services).

I'll attach sbom-redwood-202611.csv, a sample attestation JSON, and the public model signing key. Rafael, please confirm SBOM CSV is complete before we send.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Applied Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Maya — received the bundle, thank you. A couple quick clarifications for procurement/security: 

1) Emergency patch SLA: your note mentions a 48-hour mitigation guidance and 14-day patch window. For our enterprise contract we need the 14-day window to be guaranteed for critical CVEs or an explicit escalation path to provide a signed interim patch if the full patch requires longer testing. Can you confirm whether Redwood will commit to a signed interim artifact if needed?

2) On-site acceptance: the runbook lists a 48-hour acceptance window after handover. Our ops team typically requires a 5-business-day validation window to run extended smoke tests and compliance scans. Can you extend the suggested acceptance window or confirm how long we can hold acceptance sign-off before moving to production?

If you can reply with short bullet responses to those two points we'll loop in procurement and security and move forward.

Thanks,
Anna

Security Programs Lead — Elmbridge Health
